_about: College-name rules applied to the EACR adoption payload at build time: which MAP entities are sandbox (never counted or displayed), and which duplicate spellings are one institution entered twice. Consumed by excel_to_dashboard.py::_load_map_roster_rules().
_authority: Supabase public.map_colleges — `entity_kind` is the classifier, and it already tagged every row below. This file is a committed SNAPSHOT so the daily build stays hermetic (the pipeline has no Supabase read for the roster, and a build must not fail because a network call did).
_refresh: select college_id, college_name, entity_kind from map_colleges where entity_kind = 'test' order by college_name;  -- then reconcile `sandbox` below. Re-check `fold` whenever MAP adds a continuing-education or Calbright-style split entity.
_ruling: Sam, 2026-08-17: "CAlbright, etc. should only be in once and CAMAP can be left out altogether—it's our sandbox."

sandbox._why: entity_kind = 'test' in map_colleges. These are MAP's own test orgs. They must not appear as columns, must not be counted as adopters, and must not reach an export. Measured 2026-08-17: only CA MAP INITIATIVE COLLEGE was actually present in the exhibits payload — it was counted as a real adopter on the statewide card 'California Real Estate Broker License', publishing 7 adopters where the true count is 6. The other seven are listed so the rule stays correct if they ever appear.

fold._why: One institution entered under two spellings in the raw MAP export. map_colleges holds exactly ONE row for each (ids 24, 121, 119), so the duplicate is an export artifact, not a roster fact. Verified 2026-08-17: all six spellings carry ZERO adoptions, so folding cannot lose units — but the merge is written as a SUM anyway, because that stops being true the moment one of them articulates something.
fold._note: Fold maps a variant spelling onto the canonical name. The canonical must itself be a name map_colleges carries.
fold._mojibake: The fourth entry is not a duplicate ENTRY, it is a duplicate ENCODING: 'Ca\u00c3\u00b1ada College' is 'Ca\u00f1ada College' read as latin-1 and re-encoded as UTF-8. Both spellings are emitted by excel_to_dashboard.py itself, on different paths — the correct one reaches potential_names (634 cards), the mangled one reaches statewide_prescriptive.js (26 college-pairs) — so a consumer building a college axis from the payload gets TWO Ca\u00f1ada columns, one of them holding all 26 opportunities and the other empty. Found 2026-08-17 (session 165) while building the adoption matrix. It was invisible before because the only consumer resolving these names ran them through cplCollegeShort(), whose normalize() folds \u00c3\u00b1 -> n and so silently absorbed it: the label count read 118 while the underlying axis was 119. Escaped as \u here so this file's own encoding cannot corrupt the very string it is describing. The encoding defect upstream in the prescriptive builder is worth fixing at source; this fold is the safety net that must stay regardless.

map.San Diego College of Continuing Educatio: San Diego College of Continuing Education

_expected_axis._why: A regression tripwire. If these counts move, a college was added, renamed, or newly folded — which is worth noticing rather than silently rendering a different number of columns.
_expected_axis._measured_where: payload_spellings counts the RAW MAP export, before any rule. The PUBLISHED statewide_data.js is already post-sandbox (the generator drops it at build time), so counting the artifact gives 121, not 122 — that is the rules working, not a regression. after_rules is the number to assert on a consumer: 121 artifact spellings - 3 fold variants actually present = 118. Only 3 of the 4 folds fire on today's data; 'Calbright College Credit' no longer appears at all.
_expected_axis._noncredit_gap: Sam expects FOUR standalone noncredit institutions (NOCE, San Diego Cont. Ed, Mt. SAC NC, Calbright). Only three are renderable: Mt. SAC Noncredit has no separate identity in map_colleges or the exhibits export, so it cannot be a column until MAP carries it. See docs/noncredit_cpl_thinking.md and the Learning Partners roadmap row.
